standard.title: Compose using style-specific devices
standard.description: compose music, manipulating and combining elements of music and compositional devices relevant to chosen styles and/or forms to communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning and notate, document and/or record the music
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have composed music using elements and compositional devices to communicate ideas, including for collaborative and cross-curricular purposes (AC9AMU8C01/C02 — Y7-8). The Y9-10 step requires style-specific compositional devices as distinct knowledge, application of aural understanding of key and tonality, and evaluating how context affects audience response.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students compose music using style-specific elements, devices and forms to communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning, notating, documenting or recording the work.

nodes.label: Aural understanding of key and tonality
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply an aural understanding of key and tonality when improvising or composing — making tonality-conscious decisions about pitch, harmony and melodic direction.
nodes.minimum_width: Compose or improvise a short passage that demonstrates awareness of key — beginning and ending on stable pitches, with recognisable tonal centre.
nodes.typical_width: Apply aural understanding of key and tonality across composition and improvisation — choosing pitches and harmonic progressions that serve tonal coherence; making deliberate tonal choices for expressive effect (e.g. modulation, unexpected chord); recognising and using characteristic scale patterns from the chosen style.
wider: Compose in two or more tonal contexts (e.g. major and minor, or a modal scale and major) — describe how the tonal quality changes the emotional effect
Improvise over a chord progression and adjust pitch choices in response to the harmonies heard — practise aural tracking of tonal centre
nodes.hinge_reason: Aural understanding of tonality is foundational to style-specific composition — virtually all Western and many non-Western compositional devices are grounded in key and tonal relationships. Students who compose without tonal awareness produce pitch sequences that conflict with their harmonic intentions. This blocks access to chord progressions, melodic development and style-specific harmonic devices.

response_modes.reason: Aural tonality understanding is built through repeated listening and singing of scale patterns, common progressions and characteristic melodic movements in the chosen style. Singing before playing or notating keeps the aural foundation primary rather than theoretical.

success_criteria: Composes or improvises a passage with a recognisable tonal centre
Makes at least one deliberate tonal choice (e.g. avoiding an unstable pitch on a strong beat, or using a characteristic scale pattern from the style)

nodes.label: Style-specific compositional devices
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and apply compositional devices specific to a chosen style (e.g. hooks, riffs, ostinatos, specific chord progressions, characteristic rhythmic patterns) to develop and shape a composition.
nodes.minimum_width: Apply at least two style-specific devices in a composition; explain how each device is characteristic of the style.
nodes.typical_width: Use style-specific compositional devices to develop compositions — hooks, riffs, ostinatos, characteristic progressions, style-specific forms; analyse how these devices are used in existing works and apply findings in original compositions; experiment with ways to combine and manipulate elements using these devices.
wider: Analyse the compositional devices in two or three works in the chosen style and use the findings to compose a new piece — document the analytical process and the compositional decisions it informed
Re-arrange an existing piece in a contrasting style by substituting the original style's devices with the new style's equivalents — compare the effect

response_modes.reason: Style-specific device application is strongest when grounded in multiple examples from the style. Listening analytically to several works before composing — rather than applying devices from memory or instruction — builds the pattern recognition that makes device use feel natural and stylistically authentic.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Composing with style-specific devices across multiple styles (e.g. blues, film music, hip-hop, classical) develops compositional flexibility and meta-awareness of how style is constructed — skills that transfer to any subsequent compositional context.
success_criteria: Applies at least two style-specific compositional devices in an original composition
Can identify how each device is characteristic of the style by citing at least one existing example

nodes.label: Context, audience and compositional purpose
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate how different traditions, styles or contexts affect audience response and use this understanding to compose music designed for a specific audience or purpose.
nodes.minimum_width: Compose a piece with a specific audience or purpose in mind; describe at least two compositional choices made to serve that audience or purpose.
nodes.typical_width: Evaluate how context and style affect audience response; use this analysis to make deliberate compositional choices (instrumentation, dynamics, structure, style); compose for specific purposes — film/game music, social or historical themes, collaborative song cycles; notate, document or record the completed work.
wider: Compose music for a video game or film sequence — document how each compositional decision serves the narrative or interactive context, and evaluate whether the music achieves its intended effect
Compose a song cycle or set of related pieces exploring a social or historical theme — analyse how the chosen style's conventions carry the theme across the full cycle

response_modes.reason: Audience-conscious composition integrates tonal understanding, style-specific device knowledge and contextual awareness into a complete compositional act with stated purpose. The teaching investment is in helping students move from 'I composed a piece' to 'I composed this piece for this reason and these choices serve that purpose.'

success_criteria: Composes a piece with a stated audience or purpose
Can describe at least two specific compositional choices made to serve that audience or purpose, and evaluate whether they succeeded
